items.question: Why isn't this an npm package?
items.answer: Because you shouldn't be held hostage by a package maintainer. Copy-pasting means the code is yours. Forever. No external dependencies, no security surprises, and zero bloat from code you don't use.

items.question: What makes NachUI different from other libraries?
items.answer: No black boxes. Unlike traditional libraries that hide logic behind abstractions, NachUI gives you the raw source code. It's a complete Design System with tokens, patterns and guides, and you can audit, modify and extend all of it as your project evolves.

items.question: Can I use NachUI in commercial projects?
items.answer: Yes. Build anything, ship anywhere. NachUI is free and open-source. No royalties, no attribution required, and no restrictions on how you use the code once it's in your project.

items.question: How do I handle updates?
items.answer: You own the schedule. Copy improvements when you want them, or stick with your customized version. No forced npm updates breaking your production build or introducing unwanted changes.

items.question: Does it work with frameworks like Next.js or Vite?
items.answer: Perfectly. Built with React and Tailwind CSS, it's compatible with any modern environment including Next.js (App & Pages Router), Remix, Vite, Astro, and more.

items.question: How does it work with AI tools like Cursor or Claude?
items.answer: Because every component is copied directly into your repository, AI coding assistants can read, extend, and refactor your design system like any other local file. No black boxes. The docs are built for them too. There is an llms.txt index, every page is also served as raw markdown, and you can install skills that teach an agent the conventions before it writes anything.

items.question: Is NachUI built for AI agents as well as developers?
items.answer: Yes, and that was on purpose. Nothing is hidden behind a compiled package, so an agent reads exactly the same source you do. Add .md to any docs URL to get that page as markdown, point your assistant at nachui.tech/llms.txt for the whole index, or install a skill so it already knows how the components are put together. The llms.txt page has the setup for each tool.

items.question: Is it accessible?
items.answer: Always. All components follow WCAG 2.2 and WAI-ARIA standards out of the box. Keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and proper focus states are fundamental, not optional.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: Why I created this project
about.content1: I built NachUI with a simple goal: to learn.
about.content2: What started as just a couple of basic components quickly evolved. Curiosity drove me to integrate native AI capabilities, develop a full backend, build a smart CLI, and implement comprehensive testing.
about.content3: But beyond the technical growth, my goal was always to create something genuinely useful. Something free of bloat, free of lock-in, and built with absolute care.
about.content4: This project is a labor of love, what we call in Spanish "amor al arte"

sprites.title: Eight that walk
sprites.subtitle: All of them come out of the same parts table and the same skeleton: the face box, the eye line, the shoulders and the hip. That is why any of them inherits the animations for free.
sprites.explainer: Every character is a row of data, not a drawing: five slots and a short seed that packs them. Adding a haircut is eleven lines, and all eight inherit it.

themes.title: Themes on one token contract
themes.subtitle: Five presets that share the same tokens. Pick one, change the radius, the primary color or the tint of the grays, then take the CSS or the tokens with you.

presets.nachui: The theme this site runs on. Warm paper grays and a near-black primary.
presets.default: Plain neutral grays with a blue primary. A clean place to start.
presets.google: Google blue on white, with the brand colors in the feedback states.
presets.microsoft: Fluent blue, warm off-white surfaces and tight corners.
presets.mr-robot: Terminal green on black, a red primary and no rounding at all.
